aerial_fibre_methods.description: Self-supporting cable between poles â€” no messenger wire needed. Preferred for long spans. Common in South African township deployments.
aerial_fibre_methods.advantage: No earthing required; easier installation; lower theft risk (no metal)

aerial_fibre_methods.description: Fibre with integrated messenger wire. Used where poles are closely spaced.
aerial_fibre_methods.advantage: Lower cost cable; faster deployment in dense pole environments

aerial_fibre_methods.description: Fibre lashed to existing infrastructure (power lines, street lamp cables).
aerial_fibre_methods.advantage: Leverages existing infrastructure; lowest civil cost

aerial_fibre_methods.description: Shallow cutting in tar or pavement for fibre placement. Used where aerial is not viable.
aerial_fibre_methods.advantage: Less disruptive than full trenching; faster than underground

key_township_challenges.description: Aerial fibre cables in townships are vulnerable to theft (particularly metallic messenger wire) and deliberate cutting. ADSS cables (no metal) reduce theft risk significantly.
key_township_challenges.mitigation: Use of all-dielectric ADSS cables; community engagement; SLA maintenance contracts with rapid response

key_township_challenges.description: Unauthorized splicing into the network by community members or ISPs is common in townships.
key_township_challenges.mitigation: OTDR monitoring; sealed splice enclosures; GPS-tagged infrastructure

key_township_challenges.description: Existing power poles in townships are often owned by Eskom or municipalities with varying access rights and structural integrity.
key_township_challenges.mitigation: Pole access agreements; structural load assessments; self-owned pole deployment where needed

key_township_challenges.description: Low-income households struggle with monthly subscription models.
key_township_challenges.mitigation: Prepaid, daily-rate, and pay-as-you-go ISP models enabled by the infrastructure layer

key_township_challenges.description: Power outages affect active network equipment (ONTs, Wi-Fi APs). Battery backup required.
key_township_challenges.mitigation: UPS/battery backup on active nodes; solar-powered cabinets in off-grid areas
